industry_snapshot.after_paragraph: The Indian specialty chemicals market (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at about ₹1,000 billion in fiscal 2017, accounting for roughly 17% of the country's total chemicals industry [^drhp-p92]. CRISIL Research reports that the segment grew at 10–12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to 2017 and forecasts it to grow at 12–14% CAGR going forward [^drhp-p94].
industry_snapshot.rationale: Industry snapshot provides scannable context for the fragmented market.

pull_quotes.after_paragraph: Customer concentration is moderate. The top 10 customers accounted for around 59%, 57%, and 59% of revenue from operations in fiscal 2015, 2016, and 2017, respectively [^drhp-p128]. No single customer dominates, but the top decile accounts for more than half the business. The company also exports, though the scale is modest: over the past five years, total exports amounted to ₹1,068.18 lakh (₹10.68 crore), with shipments to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka [^drhp-p128].
pull_quotes.quote: The top 10 customers accounted for around 59%, 57%, and 59% of revenue from operations in fiscal 2015, 2016, and 2017, respectively.
pull_quotes.rationale: Customer concentration is a key risk; this single number captures it sharply.
